memos.scout:
I can't make a strong case for buying this one. The brief's own numbers point the other way.

The class is OPERATOR, so the base rate is roughly break-even before fees, and fees here run 1.4-5.1%. A break-even expectation minus a round trip is a losing trade on average.

The one bullish-looking figure is last-15-minute buy flow (279 buyers, net +10.38 SOL), but it sits on top of a launch structure that undermines it. Over 2,100 SOL came from 27 buyers in the first two minutes, the top 5 buyers hold 99.9% of that flow, and bundle share is 100%. Sell-to-buy ratio at graduation was 0.0006. That is concentrated, pre-coordinated buying, not broad demand, and it can stop as fast as it started.

The 30-minute return is +3.9% and drawdown from the 30-minute high is zero, but a coin with this concentration can drop sharply once the operator stops supporting it, and a 30-60 minute hold gives no time to exit a sudden unwind at a reasonable price.

Verdict: no honest case for buying now. Skip.

Sell-to-buy in that window was 0.0006, so nobody sold early, but that is typical of insiders holding until a retail wave arrives. The last 15 minutes show sell_sol of 15.05 against buy_sol of 25.43, and a 0.9% return, which is a thin move that fees of 1.4-5.1% would erase. Market cap of $33.7M on a 2,212 SOL pool with a launch bot present suggests a thin float where the operator can exit into any demand. The brief itself is the strongest warning: a bundled, operator-held curve with tiny net return gives little reason to expect a recovery from a dip.
